title: From Continuous-Time Random Walks to Laplace Tails
authors: Omer Hamdi, Stanislav Burov, Eli Barkai
abstract: During Brownian motion, the displacement is normally distributed, a classical fact aligned with the central limit theorem. However, single particle tracking in complex media such as glasses, living cells, and colloidal suspensions often reveals pronounced exponential decay of the displacement distribution, known as Laplace tails. In a short letter, two of us presented the emergence of Laplace tails in the continuous time random walk (CTRW) framework. Here, a detailed complementary study is presented. By exploring the behavior of $Q_t(n)$, the probability that exactly $n$ renewals occur during time $t$, we develop a rate function-like framework for this quantity, valid for finite $t$. We show that $Q_t(n)$ exhibits exponential tails, which in turn give rise to exponential tails of the positional probability density function $P(x,t)$. Favorable comparison to finite-time numerical simulations and asymptotic large deviation rate functions establishes the validity of our results over a wide temporal range.
summary: This work rigorously analyzes the probability distribution of particle displacements in Continuous-Time Random Walks (CTRWs), showing that while typical fluctuations follow Gaussian statistics, rare events exhibit pronounced Laplace tails. By developing a rate function framework valid at finite times, the authors provide a powerful theoretical tool to characterize anomalous diffusion in complex media.
main_problem: The study investigates the deviation of particle displacement distributions from the expected Gaussian behavior (Brownian motion) in complex media, focusing on the emergence of pronounced exponential decay known as Laplace tails.
main_result: The probability density function $P(x, t)$ for displacements in Continuous-Time Random Walks exhibits Laplace tails in the large spatial separation limit ($|x| 	o \infty$), which is quantified by a rate function $\chi_{ARF}(q)$.
method: The analysis employs advanced techniques from Large Deviation Theory (LDT), utilizing saddle point approximations and developing rate function-like frameworks for both the positional PDF $P(x, t)$ and the renewal probability $Q_t(n)$.
model_or_system: The model is the Continuous-Time Random Walk (CTRW), which describes particle diffusion in complex environments like glasses or living cells. The process is governed by random waiting times $\psi(	au)$ and subsequent jumps.
key_observables: $P(x, t)$ (positional PDF), $Q_t(n)$ (probability of exactly $n$ renewals), and the associated rate functions ($I(y)$ or $\chi(q)$).
important_parameters: Time $t$, spatial separation $|x|$, ratio $q=x/t$, and parameters defining the waiting time distribution $\psi(	au)$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on developing rate function frameworks valid for finite times, extending beyond standard asymptotic LDT results. Approximations are made using saddle point methods and Taylor expansions of $\psi(	au)$ near $	au=0$.
figures_summary: Figures compare $Q_t(n)$ across different waiting time PDFs (Erlang, sum of two exponentials) against CLT predictions and the derived Asymptotic Rate Function (ARF), demonstrating matching tail behavior. Other figures plot $P(x, t)$ showing convergence to Laplace tails.
paper_structure: The paper develops a rate function framework for $Q_t(n)$, analyzes the large deviation regime ($y=n/t$), and then extends this formalism to derive the propagator $P(x, t)$. The core is comparing theoretical predictions (ARF) against known limits (CLT) and numerical simulations across various time scales.
why_interesting: The robust derivation of non-Gaussian tails (Laplace tails) in a fundamental transport model like CTRW provides insights into anomalous diffusion regimes relevant to complex biological or glassy systems, which is crucial for understanding energy/particle transport dynamics beyond simple Brownian motion.
